transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-04
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Nina Patel (Redwood CSM), Priya Shah (CISO, Orion), David Nguyen (Head of Cloud, Orion), Maya Ortiz (Compliance Manager, Orion), Tom Becker (DevOps, Orion)

Summary: Quick posture review focused on SOC 2 / ISO alignment, Trust Center access, RBAC/SSO patterns, audit logs retention, KMS/encryption flows, and data residency constraints. Agreed to share reports, set up Trust Center access, and schedule a technical deep dive on private deployment and KMS integration.

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call if you can say name and role.
[00:07] Priya Shah: Priya Shah, CISO at Orion. Thanks Lena.
[00:09] David Nguyen: David here, head of cloud infra.
[00:11] Maya Ortiz: Maya compliance.
[00:12] Tom Becker: Tom, DevOps.
[00:14] Marco Diaz: Marco, Redwood SE.
[00:16] Nina Patel: Nina, CSM Redwood.
[00:18] Lena Park: Great. We sent a short agenda — SOC 2 artifacts, trust center access, RBAC/SSO, logs/audit, encryption/KMS, data residency. Priya, any additional priorities?
[00:29] Priya Shah: No, that's it. We just want to understand how Redwood demonstrates controls mapping, where we find evidence, and what the flow looks like for private deployments. Also curious about encryption key ownership for the private VPC case.
[00:41] Lena Park: Perfect. I'll start with the high-level — Redwood has a Type II SOC 2 report covering common criteria for security and availability, and we maintain ISO 27001 scope for our control baseline. We host a Trust Center where customers can request access to detailed artifacts and evidence. I'll paste links after.
[00:54] David Nguyen: Quick Q — is the trust center multi-tenant with per-account gating, or do we get a separate portal for dedicated customers?
[01:02] Marco Diaz: Good question. The Trust Center is a gated portal. For Dedicated or Private deployments we can grant org-level access and restrict by role. It's not a separate portal; it's the same Trust Center but with RBAC that maps to your org. There may be slight differences for on-prem installs where we provide an evidence pack.
[01:20] Priya Shah: And for on-prem, do you provide a self-hosted evidence collector or do we run scripts? How does that typically work?
[01:26] Marco Diaz: For on-prem we give a package and scripts to collect logs and config snapshots. There's sometimes manual items like interview notes which we provide as PDF artifacts. For private VPC we also have audit logs sent to your cloud bucket if you configure it — you own the bucket.
[01:41] Tom Becker: So audit logs — retention windows? We need 7 years for certain controls, but maybe that's not realistic for app token logs. What do you support?
[01:50] Lena Park: We have configurable retention in the Trust Center for exported logs; default is 90 days, can extend for Dedicated/Private customers based on contract. For archival we recommend pushing to your S3/GCS with lifecycle rules — Redwood can export JSON logs to your bucket for you to retain as long as needed.
[02:06] Maya Ortiz: That's helpful. On RBAC and SSO — we run SAML SSO in our org — how granular is the role model? Can you map to our internal LDAP groups?
[02:15] Marco Diaz: Yes, Redwood supports SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning for group mapping. Roles are pluggable: admin, viewer, auditor, model-manager, billing. You can map your LDAP/AD groups via SCIM to those roles. We also support custom roles for Dedicated customers.
[02:29] Priya Shah: Do we get audit trails of who called the API and which key was used? We need per-token lineage for certain controls.
[02:36] Marco Diaz: We log token-level request metadata — API key id, route used, model variant, latency, and region. We keep metadata in the log export; we avoid storing raw prompt text in logs by default unless configured for debugging. There are options for PII redaction.
[02:52] David Nguyen: That last part — prompt text — we need assurance that customer data isn't stored in logs. Is that in the SOC 2 scope?
[02:59] Lena Park: Yes, data handling and retention are part of the Type II. The report and control mappings explain retention policies and encryption in transit and at rest. For Private deployments you can configure the KV cache and prefix caching to be ephemeral and to disable any persistent logging of content. We'll highlight that in the artifact set.
[03:18] Priya Shah: KMS — for private installs we must own our keys. Can Redwood integrate with our KMS or do you require sharing keys?
[03:25] Marco Diaz: We support customer-managed keys in major clouds via KMS/HSM integrations. For private VPC and on-prem we can plug into your KMS. For hosted plans we manage keys but provide options for bring-your-own KMS for certain enterprise tiers. For the private package we have a documented KMS flow we can share.
[03:42] Tom Becker: Is the KMS integration automatic or do we have to run a connector? How does rotation work?
[03:48] Marco Diaz: Usually we deploy a small connector in your VPC that speaks to your KMS over private networking; rotation follows your KMS policies, and the connector refreshes credentials. We'll show an architecture diagram in the deep dive.
[03:59] Maya Ortiz: We also need information on evidence ownership for controls mapping — who's responsible at Redwood to provide artifacts, and roughly how long to deliver?
[04:07] Lena Park: Good question. For standard artifacts it's usually 2 business days to grant Trust Center access and provide PDFs. For custom evidence (env snapshots, config extracts) it can take up to a week depending on scope. We'll put owners on each action item.
[04:22] Priya Shah: Are penetration test reports included? We run internal pentests and want to see your third-party results if available.
[04:28] Nina Patel: We can provide third-party pentest summaries in the Trust Center; full reports are shared under NDA for customers that require them.
[04:36] David Nguyen: On data residency, we have EU and APAC customers that must stay in-region. Does Redwood support region pinning and model routing?
[04:44] Marco Diaz: Yes, we support region pinning and routing policies. For hosted we have regions in us-west/us-east/eu-north/ap-southeast. For private, you can host in your own region or use our dedicated capacity in a chosen region. We'll show routing policy examples — we also have automatic fallback rules if capacity is constrained.
[05:02] Tom Becker: If we do dedicated capacity in a provider region, do you still manage the nodes or do we take a managed image?
[05:08] Marco Diaz: We can do both. Dedicated capacity is hosted by Redwood but logically isolated; for fully private/on-prem we provide an image and installation scripts.
[05:16] Priya Shah: Ok, last set — controls mapping. We need a crosswalk between our internal control IDs and Redwood controls for SOC 2 and ISO. Can you produce a CSV?
[05:25] Lena Park: Yes — we have a controls matrix export that maps SOC 2 criteria to Redwood policies and where evidence lives (Trust Center link or artifact id). We'll share the CSV and a sample mapping to help you fill in your side.
[05:36] Maya Ortiz: That would be ideal. Also would like a short note to our auditors explaining how key rotation and KMS ownership works in private mode.
[05:44] Marco Diaz: We'll include an auditor-ready summary and a KMS flow diagram.
[05:48] Priya Shah: Sounds good. Any blockers on timelines? We aim to complete vendor assessment in two weeks.
[05:54] Lena Park: We can provision Trust Center access within 48 hours, SOC 2 PDF same day, and schedule the SE deep dive within the next week. That should align to your two-week window.
[06:06] David Nguyen: Perfect.
[06:07] Lena Park: Recap of next steps — Lena shares SOC 2 and Trust Center invite; Marco schedules architecture deep dive; Maya shares Orion controls matrix; David confirms regions and Tom will coordinate buckets for log export.
[06:21] Priya Shah: Thanks all.
[06:23] Nina Patel: I'll follow up with calendar invites and the Trust Center link.
[06:27] Lena Park: Great, we'll send action items and mark owners. Thanks everyone, talk soon.

End of transcript. Note: occasional transcription errors present (e.g., 'KV cash' instead of 'KV cache' in some auto-notes).
